parsed.explanation: The combined regime gives a trans visitor several universal exposures: entry document rules (M/F-only markers, visa refusal on sex doubt, fraud/lifetime-ineligibility leverage, passports blocked), a facilities ban attached by the national legislature to this district, and national custody policies (conversion therapy, hormone removal, men's-ward placement, immigration abuse). Outing consequences reach arrest (documented restroom trespass arrest, men's-ward holding) and severe custody harm. Mitigants exist — courts partially enjoin orders, a hate-crime statute, active litigation, no presentation offence — but the harshest operative rules govern, and the district's protective reputation is explicitly overrideable.

entry_documents.exposure: Universal: Feb 2025 M/F-only marker policy upheld Nov 2025; X-markers halted; trans travelers report confiscated/blocked passports; visa cable orders refusal where sex is in doubt and invites fraud/lifetime-ineligibility findings; eight-plus governments issued advisories for trans citizens.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports valid until expiry; fraud finding requires four elements with limited waiver and is never automatic; ACLU suit pending; legal-aid FAQ maintained.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry refusal or investigation can cascade into detention, facility placement and care exposure under national rules.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented: restroom-trespass arrest (March 2025) with 24 hours held in men's ward; activists arrested Dec 2024; national corrections conversion-therapy policy (hair cutting, hormone removal); immigration custody forced labour, beatings, solitary, sexual abuse of trans men; prisoner counts withheld since 2025.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Trespass requires willful entry plus refusal to leave; hate-crime statute; courts have blocked some orders; pending litigation.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A service refusal or entry dispute can escalate to arrest, then birth-sex custody placement under national corrections policy.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Facilities ban attached to this district by the national legislature (scope unsourced); nationally 9+1 units ban identity-congruent facility use in all government buildings, 6 units reach private settings, 4 units criminalize use; courts upheld bans despite challenges.
federal_state_facilities.protection: District's local legislature has no ban of its own; exemptions exist in the trespass statute; a July 2026 assessment lists the district among low-risk units.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Local tolerance cannot override the national legislature's attached ban or national executive orders.

care_services.exposure: Minors' gender-affirming care banned in 27 units and framed nationally as 'mutilation'; hospital records subpoenaed; crisis-lifeline LGBTQ services shut; public insurance exclusion proposed — a travelling family's minor faces care denial if outed.
care_services.protection: Several executive orders blocked or enjoined; adult emergency care not shown to be nationally excluded; suit over October 2025 rules pending.
care_services.interaction: Care-seeking can trigger documentation review, outing and facility placement.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: DOJ cash rewards memo invoking 'radical gender ideology'; May 2026 counterterrorism strategy targeting groups 'radically pro-transgender'; law-enforcement investigation of schools over 'gender ideology'; official framing treats trans advocacy as threat-adjacent.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Reward never lists gender ideology as a criterion; strategy states counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; advocates' genocide-stage comparisons are advocacy characterizations.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Raises outing probability and official suspicion at any encounter, but no documented sweeps of trans visitors.

minors_guardians.exposure: A parent travelling with a trans minor faces unit-level care bans, prosecution-linked EO on social transition, hospital record subpoenas, and facility rules in schools/government buildings reaching the child.
minors_guardians.protection: Several orders enjoined; district itself ranked low-risk; no documented prosecution of visiting parents.
minors_guardians.interaction: Child's status can draw school/medical records scrutiny into the parent's visa and document review.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No documented organized targeting or police sweeps of trans visitors; state threat-framing and 4 criminalizing units set a hostile ambient climate; hate incidents against sexual orientation are a small share of reported bias incidents.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; 22 units plus capital outlaw identity discrimination; courts convict in bias cases (parent-level record); no trans-specific killing campaign documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police response to an assault depends on unit-level statutes (23 units cover identity); the district is not shown to be among the hostile ones.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: District's attached ban scope, enforcement beyond Dec 2024 arrests, local custody conditions, local police practice and marker-change rules are all unsourced; low-risk ranking criteria unverifiable; national posture shifts with litigation outcomes.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Functioning courts have enjoined multiple orders; ACLU passport suit pending; legal-aid FAQ and equality maps provide traveller guidance; assessment places district among low-risk units.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies operate at national level and are contestable but currently incomplete; oversight findings have not reversed the passport or custody policies.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than 0.35-A: Veluna has one universal facility rule and polite streets; this dossier adds a universal entry document/visa regime with fraud leverage, documented custody conversion therapy and immigration abuse, and state threat-framing — more universal exposures and worse post-outing severity, partially offset by working courts.

Lower than 0.45-D: Veleda's exposure is transport searches plus isolated facility issues; here the entry document regime, criminalizing units, custody harm and care restrictions stack across the whole journey, though like Veleda there is no presentation offence or police campaign.

Higher than 0.25-D: Savorek combines universal ward rules, routine police extortion and rejected complaints with functioning hostile institutions; this dossier has comparable facility/custody exposure but no documented routine police extortion or stops of visitors, plus courts that partially grant relief.

parsed.synthesis: The district's own profile is comparatively mild — no local ban, low-risk ranking, no documented local police hostility — but the combined operative regime is national: the passport/visa document regime reaches every trans traveller at processing, the national legislature's facilities ban sits inside the district and cannot be repealed locally, and national corrections/immigration custody policies impose hormone removal, birth-sex placement and documented abuse if the traveller is detained. Litigation partly blunts these rules but has not reversed the document or custody policies. Severity after outing (arrest, custody abuse, care denial for a minor) plus universal entry exposure places this well below the reduced-risk bands; functioning courts and civil society keep it above the organised-targeting tier.
